stances_toward.note: Adversary is our reading, and no source uses the word. The structure is mortal: JNIM fights to take the state's territory and the junta fights to destroy the group, so each side's aim is the other's defeat. The Barsalogho attack (August 2024) is the dated marker; the start of the war is not dated here. Mirror: the BEN card's ACLED source says JNIM uses Tapoa and Kompienga provinces in Burkina Faso for raids into Benin; that is about the group's use of Burkinabe ground, not an act of the state. Bond grievance is our reading of an open war with massacres on both sides. Gaps: the Djibo attack is not verified (the search found only Barsalogho); the junta's own casualty figures are not published here.

stances_toward.note: Adversary, the only mortal enemy on this card. JNIM's stated aim is to replace state authority with its own interpretation of Islamic law (CSIS), so the junta's existence is at stake, not only its territory. The fuel blockade of Bamako from September 2025 and the army's airstrikes in reply are the evidence of the war. No source uses the word adversary: this is our reading and the reason it is rare. Bond none.

stances_toward.note: Mortal enemy in Tillabéri, on the structural reading: JNIM fights the state's forces and its airport, and the junta's stated aim is the defeat of the armed groups on its soil; the sources describe continuous attacks, not a declared aim of the group's wish to end the state, so the grade rests on the continuity of the war. Sources are tier 3 and the grade is ours; the rivalry with ISSP (ACLED, via ADF) raises the stakes but is not the grade's basis. Stable: attacks recur through 2026 in the same provinces. Bond grievance: an open war with no channel of talks in any source. Gap: the start of the war is not dated in these sources; since is the earliest dated JNIM attack in them (the March 2026 Banibangou convoy ambush, reported as JNIM and ISSP).

relations_to.summary: JNIM attack on Barsalogho (Kaya province, 24 August 2024): up to 200 killed and at least 140 injured, mostly civilians and militia members digging trenches beside soldiers. The junta condemned the attack without a casualty figure for its own forces. ACLED says JNIM uses Tapoa and Kompienga provinces in Burkina Faso as staging grounds for raids into Benin; the row records the group's use of Burkinabe ground, not a state act.
relations_to.note: Death tolls differ by source; the range is recorded, not one number. The Djibo attack is not verified: the search returned nothing on it. The ACLED source is mirrored from the BEN card, which holds the Benin side of the same spillover.

relations_to.summary: JNIM attacked Niamey's international airport, which hosts Air Base 101 and the Africa Corps, on about 18 June 2026, three days after ISSP's assault on the military bases at Inates and Banibangou; the attack killed 11 soldiers and two civilians, according to ADF Magazine. The attribution and toll rest on tier-3 reporting.
